questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to choose an English speaking country as enhancing my legal English was on the top of my list. In addition, I wanted to be able to easily communicate with fellow students and acquaintances. Studying in a big international city has always been a dream of mine, so London was the perfect match. Furthermore, knowing that the level of academics was at a decent level was also important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's been the perfect experience both on a social and academic level. I have gotten so many new perspectives on law, but also on life in general. The way you live in London will always be a part of me and something that will inspire me going forward.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say it was relatively easy, but bear in mind that you are arriving at a completely new institution, so it feels like starting over again. So, the first few days was a bit confusing navigating between the different systems at Queen Mary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had study abroad "officer's" to guide us if anything was needed, and otherwise you receive frequent newsletters via. email up to arrival, and after you arrive. In those letters there is everything you need to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There could definitely be a more easy and manageable way of doing it. There wasn't really a centralized information source other than the newsletters, so it is really important that you read these.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: London is a tough choice for housing, but most bigger cities in Europe can be challenging, so start your search maybe three / four months ahead. There is not a lot of affordable options for students and especially if you want to live in a nice area. However, I lived at KFUK a danish student home in Hampstead, which is very affordable and nicely placed. A bit far away from campus, but I could really recommend applying for that. Otherwise, consider finding housing in East London as that will make your commute to campus way shorter. You unfortunately can't live on campus at Queen Mary.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is nice as you get to "choose" where to live in London, but might become a bit lonely if you don't socialize in the beginning at Queen Mary. That is why I appreciated living at KFUK since you get connected with many other danish students that study at different universities in London. Again, finding housing in East London e.g. Shoreditch, Bethnal Green, Hackney could also be good, as campus will be very close, but might be expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You aren't able to live on campus at Queen Mary so this makes it a bit difficult to give it a high rating. However, maybe you can get lucky and text the Housing Team at Queen Mary closer to arrival, if any of their housing is available or for tips.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. However, there are many deadlines regarding module registration and different processes so note all this down.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
1. Pre-registration (where you get to choose modules - choose them the same day they become available to make sure you get the ones you want).
2. Module registration (this is where you get notified if you got your modules).
3. Add / drop period (typically in September at intro week and the couple of weeks following, where you have the chance to add or drop modules if you are not satisfied).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Queen Mary study abroad team is ready to assist here, and I emailed them a couple of times about modules, and they replied within a couple of hours to a day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful I got all the modules I wanted, I think the key is to apply right when the registration opens as some modules have limited space for exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of the deadlines.
2. Make sure to choose modules ASAP.
3. You can always try to get new or drop modules in the add / drop period in the beginning (so no stress).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
At Queen Mary module courses are divided into level 4 (equivalent to first year),5 (second year) or 6 (third year) for bachelor students. 

Some of my courses were challenging me, mostly the level 6 course I chose. The other courses I had on level 4 and 5 were interesting, but quite easy and manageable academically. So if you appreciate a "high level" might be the best to only choose level 6 (or 5) courses if possible.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Definitely quite similar. The tutors are informal and easy to approach. The seminars are called tutorials and only last one hour so that feels a bit short, and lectures are often two hours. Books are available online via. LawTrove, so no need for those expenses, which is quite nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Competition Law (Level 6)
2. Internet Law (level 5)
3. Business Law (level 5)
4. Contract Law (Level 4)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Internet Law - a very passionate and interesting tutor on this module. The lectures are great with good and exam friendly slides. The module engages with various different issues regarding the internet and law e.g. Data protection, Criminal Law on hacking, intellectual property & AI etc.

Competition Law - an interesting module if you appreciate EU law and is interested in competition between companies in general. Can be quite heavy on reading and case law, but this also makes it academically challenging, which I appreciated. Only one hour of teaching a week, so this makes your schedule more free, but also requires you to self-study a bit more. The exam is not too difficult.

Business Law - hands down the best tutor on Queen Mary, super passionate and is very good at delivering lectures in an interesting and different way. He engages with students in his teaching, is friendly and much well-connected in the area between law and business. However, the module is a bit general and "high-flying" on legal subjects, but it provides a basic view into the legal English system and common law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really most of my costs were accounted for in the budget.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food - this can be very expensive. However, I lived at KFUK where you get 10 free meals a month which helped on the budget.
Drinking - It is quite expensive to go out in London, probably similar to Copenhagen and sometimes even more expensive.
Transportation - As a Queen Mary student you are very dependent on the tube (metro) and this turned out to be a lot more expensive than expected. I can recommend getting a Student Oyster Card (apply right when you arrive!) for a fixed fee, so this will not worry you all the time.
Books at Uni - These are "free" as all the books that are a part of the curriculum for the module is available on LawTrove.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Queen Mary offers a lot of opportunities for joining societies, I think there might be over 100 different ones. So join in!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Many sports clubs (football, basketball, american football, tennis, karate etc.)
Legal clubs (enter into competitions, network opportunities etc.)
Nationality societies (Caribbean, Turkish, Pakistani, Nordic etc.)
Debating societies 
AND many more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was a part of the tennis society which was very good. You can join in at every level (beginner, intermediate or competitive). They have practice two times a week on outdoor courts. They offer fun socials too where you get the opportunity to network with other students. The tennis society provided me with many friends (also ones that are not exchange students).

I was also a part of the Nordic Society which offers good chances of pub quizzing, club nights etc. This is a chance for you to connect with other nordic students (Swedish, Finnish, Icelandic etc.) studying at Queen Mary, but sometimes bigger events include students from LSE, Kings College, Royal Holloway etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
At Queen Mary there is reading week, which is a full week where you don't have studies at all (a part from the reading you do one your own), so this is a great opportunity to go on a longer trip. I myself went to Edinburgh in Scotland which was a fun experience.

I also went to Cornwall which is south in England (probably go early on your trip, so start / mid September). Cornwall offers beaches, cliffs, beautiful oceans, local pubs and in general beautiful nature. I visited the cities Newquay (surfers hotspot) and Padstow (cute little city with a lot of good seafood).

Otherwise fun day trips could be Oxford or Cambridge which is quite close to London. I went to Oxford which was so cool as the city is impressive and aesthetic especially the University.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found this quite easy, English culture is not too far away from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies! This is almost the only way or be very open in the beginning of your modules to find mates within your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Pub culture! There are so many in London and they offer great ways of socialising. 
The creative scene! Many museums are free or you can join on student memberships. I also watched shows at the Royal Ballet and Opera House which was nice. London is also a hotspot for music with many interesting artists coming by.
Sports! Watch your favorite premier league team or see NBA / NFL in London.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Socialize in the beginning. Friends are not easily made at Queen Mary and initiatives from the university are not the best other than the voluntary intro week. So, be proactive and make your connections.
2. Plan your time - this is in general a good idea, but Queen Mary has a very sharp deadline for exams, all assignments need to be submitted by 12 th of December, and some of your exam questions will be available from start December. So, this is really a busy period, so be focused on planning your time here. Otherwise, the other parts of the semester is pretty chill at Queen Mary.
3. Timetables - in the beginning when you get your timetable for modules you might have clashes. This can be frustrating and Queen Mary is not always the best to solve this, but take it chill and follow the guidance provided.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Queen Mary itself with the Mile End Campus is not the prettiest. However, it is functional and the campus has everything you need.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: In general, just being in a different country and getting new perspectives on life and academics.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
In the beginning reading in English as the legal academic books can be a bit of a challenge.
Socialising - don't think too much just connect with others all are there to make friends. I was maybe a bit slow at the start.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO ON THE EXCHANGE! You will not regret it (even if you don't choose Queen Mary).

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
